title: Which seeds have the most omega-3?

seo.title: Seeds highest in omega-3: flax, chia, and hemp
seo.meta_description: Flax and chia are rich in ALA omega-3. Compare them with hemp and learn why plant ALA is not equivalent gram for gram to fish EPA and DHA.
seo.search_intent: Compare seeds by omega-3 content while distinguishing plant ALA from the EPA and DHA found in fish.

excerpt: Flax and chia clearly stand out for ALA omega-3. NIH lists about 2.35 g ALA in a tablespoon of whole flaxseed and 5.06 g in one ounce of chia. Hemp also contributes ALA, but at a lower concentration.
content_html:
When seeds are described as rich in omega-3, the specific fat is usually ALA, alpha-linolenic acid. That distinction matters because fatty fish mainly provide EPA and DHA, and the body converts only a limited amount of ALA into those long-chain omega-3s.

The seeds that stand out

SeedApproximate ALAUseful serving example
Flaxseed~20–23 g/100 g1 tbsp whole flax: ~2.35 g ALA
Chia~18 g/100 g1 oz: ~5.06 g ALA
Hulled hemp~8–9 g/100 g1 oz: roughly ~2.3–2.5 g ALA
Pumpkin seedsfar lowerbetter known for magnesium and zinc

The exact values vary by variety and database entry, but the broad ordering is stable: flax and chia sit in the top tier.

Small servings provide a lot of ALA

NIH lists 5.06 g ALA in one ounce of chia, equivalent to roughly 18.1 g per 100 g. A tablespoon of whole flaxseed provides about 2.35 g.

For context, the U.S. Adequate Intake for ALA is 1.6 g/day for adult men and 1.1 g/day for adult women. Those are reference intakes rather than personalized prescriptions, but they show why a modest serving of chia or flax can contribute a substantial amount.

ALA is not the same as EPA plus DHA

The body can convert ALA to EPA and then DHA, but NIH describes the conversion as very limited, with reported conversion to long-chain forms below 15% and conversion to DHA lower still.

That means 2 g ALA from seeds should not be presented as equivalent to 2 g EPA+DHA from salmon. They belong to the same omega-3 family, but they are not interchangeable gram for gram.

Does flax need to be ground?

Whole flaxseed can pass through partly intact, while grinding breaks the seed coat and exposes its interior. Chia is commonly eaten whole or hydrated; its fiber forms a gel without requiring the same mechanical step.

Hemp contributes omega-3 and a lot of protein

Hulled hemp seed contains roughly 31–32 g protein and about 49 g fat per 100 g. Its ALA concentration is below flax and chia, but a one-ounce serving can still provide roughly 2.3–2.5 g.

The useful takeaway

Flax and chia are the standout seeds for ALA; hemp is a meaningful but less concentrated source. A useful omega-3 comparison always states which omega-3 is being measured instead of treating plant ALA and marine EPA/DHA as the same thing.

faq.question: Which seed has the most omega-3?
faq.answer: Flax and chia are among the most concentrated common seeds for ALA. Exact ranking depends on the specific database entry.

faq.question: Is chia omega-3 the same as salmon omega-3?
faq.answer: No. Chia mainly provides ALA; salmon provides EPA and DHA. Only a limited amount of ALA is converted to long-chain omega-3s.

faq.question: Does hemp contain omega-3?
faq.answer: Yes. Hulled hemp provides ALA, though at a lower concentration than flax or chia.
